subject.title: [Feature]: Thread replies when agent uses tools; top-level for conversational responses

question: Should Slack add a default-off tool-use-sensitive reply policy, and what precedence should it have relative to static `replyToMode`, per-channel overrides, DMs/group DMs, existing threads, explicit top-level opt-outs, streaming previews, and status indicators?
rationale: Current source shows the requested behavior is absent, but adding it changes operator-visible Slack delivery configuration and reply placement policy, which needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
options.body: Define the config shape and precedence, then implement the Slack-owned schema, routing, docs, and tests with default false for upgrade safety.

options.title: Use static reply controls only
options.body: Treat account, chat-type, and per-channel `replyToMode` as the supported channel-cleanliness controls and close this direction as not planned.

options.title: Defer to broader reply policy design
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers design a cross-channel reply-placement policy instead of adding a Slack-only heuristic.

recommendation.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
recommendation.body: Define the config shape and precedence, then implement the Slack-owned schema, routing, docs, and tests with default false for upgrade safety.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history on the overlapping Slack reply-mode implementation and merge decision.
